title: Bouncing ball

caveats: ball stretches vertically during fast fall and squashes on impact

reference.basis: ten alternating black-white bands count as a standard 1.0 m metre stick

slow_motion.evidence: No narration, captions or on-screen text indicate slow motion.

subjects.description: small glossy blue spherical ball falling and bouncing vertically

observation.what_happens: A blue ball drops from just below the striped bar at the top and falls vertically to the brown floor. It bounces up and falls again repeatedly, drifting slightly rightward, until it settles on the floor.

calibration.note: black and white striped bar = 1 m (ten alternating black-white bands count as a standard 1.0 m metre stick) spans 480 px in SAM's mask

given: scale: black and white striped bar = 1 m (ten alternating black-white bands count as a standard 1.0 m metre stick) spans 480 px in SAM's mask, known to ±1%
reasoning: y drops ~0.92 m in ~0.9 s then rebounds to ~0.46 m and ~0.23 m implying e~0.7, while x drifts right steadily at ~0.1 m/s. Candidates test pure gravity bounce versus weak linear viscous drag versus quadratic turbulent drag with sideways bounce friction to predict the later settling bounces.

law.summary: The ball falls under gravity and bounces off the floor losing the same fraction of speed each time, with no air slowing it.

caveats: Scale rests on the striped bar being exactly one metre, good to about one percent.
Sideways drift is treated as steady gliding, so any spin or curve is ignored.
Tiny final settle rolls may not bounce as cleanly as the big hops.
critique.finding: The ball drops under gravity {g} and hits the floor at {y_floor}. Each bounce keeps {e} of its upward speed, with no air slowing it.
critique.headline: The ball falls freely; the air barely touches it.
critique.why_it_won: It nails every bounce without needing any air drag, while the draggy model adds extra slowing the ball never shows.

headline: The ball falls freely; the air barely touches it.
finding: The ball drops under gravity 2.44 ± 0.025 m/s² and hits the floor at -0.956 ± 0.0096 m. Each bounce keeps 0.7 ± 0.00056 of its upward speed, with no air slowing it. That is 4× weaker than Earth’s gravity, so the clip most likely plays about 2× slower than real life.

eyeball.law_in_words: vertical motion is constant acceleration due to gravity with free-fall position proportional to t squared, and at floor contact the vertical velocity reverses and is scaled by the normal restitution e

clock.note: Gravity came out 4× too weak. Either this happened somewhere with 0.25× Earth’s gravity, or the clip plays about 2× slower than real life (slow motion). Run it again with the slow-motion factor set.
